context:
Render from per-result detail JSON files. Pre-render at build time for SEO
and fast loading. Enhance with JS for sorting, charts, and companion files.
Keep the page layout clean and scannable - metadata at top, query table
prominent, companion data expandable.
description:
Build the result detail page at `/results/r/{result_id}`. This is the
canonical public page for a single benchmark result - the page users share,
link to, and bookmark. It shows full metadata, per-query timing breakdown,
validation status, environment info, and a download link to the raw bundle.

This is the Geekbench "result page" equivalent for BenchBox. Every result in
the corpus gets a stable, pre-rendered detail page.

anti_patterns.dont: compute aggregate statistics on the detail page that aren't in the source data
anti_patterns.why: the detail page shows one result truthfully

anti_patterns.dont: require JavaScript to see basic result data
anti_patterns.why: pre-rendered HTML is better for SEO and sharing

preserves.behavior: Every detail page must link to the raw canonical schema-v2 bundle for download
Pre-rendered HTML must show full metadata and query table without JavaScript

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run build && ls dist/r/*/index.html | wc -l
verifications.description: Vite build succeeds and detail pages are pre-rendered

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && grep -c '<td>' dist/r/$(ls dist/r/ | head -1)/index.html
verifications.description: Pre-rendered detail pages contain query table without JavaScript

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run typecheck && npm run build

work_units.notes:
The detail page for `/results/r/{result_id}` shows:

Header section:
- Benchmark name + platform name (large, prominent)
- Scale factor, date, total duration
- Trust badge: "Maintainer Run" (Phase 1 only has this label)
- "Download Raw Bundle" button linking to the canonical schema-v2 JSON

Metadata panel:
- Environment: OS, arch, CPU count, memory
- Configuration: compression, tuning mode, validation mode, phases run
- Query summary: N passed, N failed, total queries

Data source: per-result detail JSON from `details/{result_id}.json`
work_units.summary: Implement the result detail page layout and metadata display

work_units.notes:
Show per-query results in a sortable table:
| Query | Time (ms) | Rows | Status |
|-------|-----------|------|--------|
| Q1    | 45.2      | 4    | passed |
| Q2    | 12.1      | 460  | passed |
...

Add a simple bar chart showing query times (horizontal bars, sorted by
query ID or by duration). This can be a lightweight SVG/Canvas chart -
no need for a charting library. The chart gives visual context that the
table alone doesn't provide.

Highlight failed queries in red. Show validation details if available.
work_units.summary: Implement the query timing table and visualization

work_units.notes:
If the result has companion files (.plans.json, .tuning.json):
- Show a "Query Plans" expandable section with plan text per query
- Show a "Tuning Configuration" section with applied tuning clauses
- Link to companion file downloads

If companions are not available, hide the sections cleanly.
work_units.summary: Add companion file display (query plans, tuning config)

work_units.notes:
- "Compare with another result" button that navigates to compare view
  with this result pre-selected
- Breadcrumb: Results > TPC-H > DuckDB > This Result
- "Other results for this benchmark" and "Other results on this platform"
  quick links (from manifest data)
work_units.summary: Add compare action and navigation context

work_units.notes:
During Vite build, read manifest.json and generate static HTML for every
result: `/results/r/{result_id}/index.html`. Each page includes the full
metadata and query table in the HTML (no JS required for basic content).
JavaScript enhances with sorting, charts, and companion file display.
work_units.summary: Pre-render detail pages at build time
